method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP) 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease' (published 21 April 2026). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13288312). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Diagnose clinically or genetically.** Screen at-risk adults with ultrasound; use CT or MRI when the result is unclear or for prognosis. Counsel people before screening about what it may show.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Genomic testing is publicly funded in Australia** (MBS item 74 301, for suspected monogenic cystic kidney disease) but only a nephrologist or clinical geneticist can request it, and genetic counselling comes first. New Zealand has no public subsidy.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A negative genetic test does not exclude a genetic cause:** PKD1 pseudogenes and exome-based panels can miss the variant. If suspicion stays high, consider further testing such as whole-genome sequencing.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood pressure follows the KDIGO 2021 BP-in-CKD guideline**, though the ADPKD targets differ. Home BP monitoring is a practical substitute for ambulatory monitoring, notably by telehealth in rural and remote areas.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic kidney pain (over 3 months):** first rule out other causes and acute events such as cyst rupture. Step up from paracetamol and heat, to TENS or acupuncture, to spinal cord stimulation, to nephrectomy; refractory pain needs a multidisciplinary team.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for UTI when there is fever, flank or acute abdominal pain, a raised white count or raised CRP.** Australian guidance gives nitrofurantoin for 5 days, but not in CKD G3–G5. Infected kidney cysts need a lipid-soluble antibiotic given for longer.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Standard CKD care applies, with two exceptions:** SGLT2 inhibitors are not advised for now, and HIF-PHIs are not recommended for anaemia, because trials excluded people with ADPKD.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transplant is the preferred kidney replacement therapy.** Living donation gives better outcomes, but related donors need genetic testing, which may limit who can donate.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat polycystic liver disease by symptoms and severity;** do not over-treat people without symptoms. Somatostatin analogues suit a markedly enlarged liver with severe symptoms but are not publicly funded here. Counsel on hormone effects (including contraception) on liver volume.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not screen everyone for intracranial aneurysm.** Screen (time-of-flight MRA without gadolinium, or CT angiography) with a family history of aneurysm or subarachnoid haemorrhage, a high-risk job such as pilot, major surgery, or marked anxiety. Keep known unruptured aneurysms under surveillance.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **KDIGO: start tolvaptan in adults with eGFR ≥ 25 mL/min/1.73m2 who are at risk of rapid progression** (Mayo class 1C–1E, or eGFR falling by ≥3 mL/min per 1.73 m2 a year). CARI endorses this plus the more detailed ERA-EDTA algorithm for identifying rapid progressors for subsidy.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use shared decision-making, especially over age 55,** where there is no trial evidence. Start at the lowest split dose and titrate under physician supervision with nephrologist input.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Liver injury is a serious risk: test LFTs monthly for 18 months, then quarterly.** Expect thirst, polyuria and nocturia; make sure fluid intake is enough, especially in hot weather.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No other drug is recommended to slow ADPKD:** not mTOR inhibitors, statins, somatostatin analogues, metformin or complementary medicines, because the evidence is insufficient.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep sodium under 2 g a day (87 mmol) and protein at 0.8 g/kg** to reduce urine output modestly, particularly on tolvaptan. Refer to a kidney-specialised dietitian. Special diets, including ketogenic diets, have no evidence.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drink 2–3 L/day, mainly water, if eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2,** adjusted for the person and climate. Moderate caffeine (<400 mg per day) is fine.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Obesity is linked to faster progression.** Refer for weight management (with care to avoid malnutrition in CKD G4–G5) and encourage more than 150 min/week of exercise plus 1 h of strength training.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy is not contraindicated,** but risk rises with reduced kidney function, uncontrolled hypertension or past pre-eclampsia. Offer pre-pregnancy counselling and multidisciplinary care. ⚠️ **Stop tolvaptan before conception** (teratogenic).
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In pregnancy, target BP ≤130/85 mmHg** (<135/85 mmHg with pre-existing hypertension), and give low-dose aspirin 75–150 mg/day, ideally in the evening, from week 12 to 36.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not screen children without symptoms by ultrasound.** Test only when indicated (for example hypertension or haematuria) under a paediatric nephrologist; check BP in every child with or at risk of ADPKD.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23
